commands.result: hostapd 2.11 reached AP-ENABLED with the room's 32-character hexadecimal WLAN SSID, the LDN RSN IE in the beacon/probe response, and no association-response RSN IE. The wrapper created the mon-ldn monitor vif on the same phy and ran the advertisement and 0x88B7 responder. The run was interrupted at about eight seconds, after the console had already authenticated, associated, and disassociated; the harness did not print its final summary.
Rejected by the wrapper before any radio action because the wrapper must run as the normal user and uses sudo internally.

hostapd_log.summary: The console completed open-system authentication, associated with AID 1, and reached AP-STA-CONNECTED with authorized=1. About one second later hostapd received a disassociation from the console with reason_code=8, logged AP-STA-DISCONNECTED, and later deauthenticated the station due to inactivity.
hostapd_log.note: The log contains the console's authentication request (len=41), association request (len=127), association response TX status, and disassociation. It does not contain an EAPOL or 0x88B7 exchange. The association response omitted the RSN IE for this run.

interpretation: The WLAN layer succeeded again: the console authenticated, associated with AID 1, and hostapd marked the station authorized. The console then sent one null-data frame and disassociated itself with reason 8 about 1.4 seconds after association, before any 0x88B7 authentication request. Omitting the association-response RSN IE did not change the outcome, so that mismatch is not the cause. The pcap shows no console data payload frame at all, only the null-data frame, so the console did not reach the custom LDN exchange. The leading remaining host-side difference is the beacon SSID encoding: hostapd sends a zero-length SSID, while the ldn package's MonitorAP sends 32 zero bytes. The probe response to the console carries the real 32-byte SSID, so the probe path matches the reference. Other untested differences include capability information, the extended-capabilities IE, and hostapd's WLAN state machine versus the reference MonitorAP. The console stayed responsive, so there is no evidence of a memory-safety fault.
limitations: The run was interrupted at about eight seconds, so the full 90-second window was not observed. The console had already disassociated by then.
No independent receiver captured the AP's transmissions; the monitor pcap is on the same phy and may include loopback.
The console reaction is owner-reported and was not instrumented.
No 0x88B7 authentication request was observed; the run cannot distinguish a console abort before the request from a receive-path miss.
The disassociation cause is not proven. The beacon SSID difference is a candidate, not a demonstrated cause.
One adapter, driver, kernel, and channel.
